claim: In early 1895, the U.S. Treasury's gold reserve had fallen to roughly $42 million, far below the $100 million floor set by the 1875 Resumption Act, during the depression that followed the Panic of 1893. On February 8, 1895, President Grover Cleveland's administration contracted with a private banking syndicate led by J.P. Morgan and August Belmont & Co. to deliver gold worth slightly more than $65 million in exchange for about $62.4 million in 30-year U.S. bonds, restoring the reserve above $100 million. August Belmont & Co. was the American agent of the Rothschild banking house; the formal contracting parties included N.M. Rothschild & Sons of London, and Cleveland's own message to Congress stated that at least half the gold would be supplied from abroad. A foreign-linked private syndicate underwriting the solvency of the federal government, at a profit it never publicly disclosed, drew sustained attack from silverite Democrats and populists; William Jennings Bryan carried that grievance into the 'cross of gold' politics of the 1896 campaign.

sources.label: Miller Center, University of Virginia — Grover Cleveland, “Announcement of Treasury Bond Sale,” February 8, 1895 (text of the president's message).
sources.quote: At least one-half of the gold to be obtained is to be supplied from abroad, which is a very important and favorable feature of the transaction.

sources.label: Encyclopedia.com — “Morgan-Belmont Agreement.” Identifies the February 8, 1895 contract and August Belmont as the American representative of the Rothschilds of Paris.
sources.quote: American representative of the Rothschilds of Paris

sources.label: Wikipedia — “Panic of 1893.” Names the contracting parties to the 1895 bond syndicate (Drexel, Morgan & Co.; A. Belmont & Co.; J.S. Morgan & Co.; N.M. Rothschild & Sons).
HistoryNet — “Upside-Down Bailout.” On the political backlash, Bryan's “cross of gold” attack, and Morgan declining to disclose the syndicate's profit.

notes: Opens the era-i finance spine that the y1913 Jekyll Island and Federal Reserve records continue. 'August Belmont' in 1895 is August Belmont Jr.; the Rothschild agency in America dates to his father, the firm's founder. The $65M (gold delivered) vs $62.4M (bond face value) figures are two sides of the same transaction, both in Cleveland's message — not a contradiction. The syndicate's profit was never publicly disclosed (Morgan declined to answer); contemporary press estimates (~$5M, New York World) are attributed claims, not audited figures, so the claim says only 'a profit it never publicly disclosed.' Primary quote (Miller Center) confirmed verbatim. Surfaced via capture DWS2NxBjV8U.
